family: Citation and claim verification (support / contradict / silent)
source: Verification beside a generative system (build specification pattern table)
description: Measures whether the model can place a claim against a source excerpt in one of three relations (supports, contradicts, silent), whether it can separate answer evidence from premise contradiction for a retrieved passage, and whether it can flag a per field extraction error including a wrongly empty field. The discriminating axis is the silent class: a third of the relation cases are claims the excerpt neither states nor denies while sharing its vocabulary, so a model that collapses plausible onto supports loses silent recall. Gold labels never depend on arithmetic, counting, or date differences; every label is settled by reading two adjacent sentences. Scores are deliberately absent because strength of support has no unambiguous gold level. The fabricated quote case from the citation cookbook is also absent: code verifies the quoted string before any model call, so it is not a model question. Report a three class confusion matrix for the relation choices plus noul accuracy at 0.5, not a single number: a supports and contradicts confusion and a supports and silent confusion are different defects.

cases.name: change-record-long
cases.rationale: The rollback operator sits in the middle of a long record, the clock skew cause is never given, and the record states no invoices were delayed.

state.source_excerpt: Change record CR-4482 covers the migration of the billing scheduler from the legacy cron host to the managed job runner. The change window opened at 22:00 on 4 May and the scheduler was drained of queued jobs before any configuration was touched. Priya Raghavan performed the cutover and Tomas Lind observed from the incident channel. Fifteen minutes after cutover the managed runner began reporting duplicate job identifiers, so Priya executed the documented rollback to the legacy cron host and confirmed that the queue drained normally. Tomas opened follow up ticket OPS-1190 to investigate the duplicate identifiers before a second attempt. The postmortem meeting was scheduled for 7 May. No customer invoices were delayed, because the billing run for that evening had already completed before the change window opened. The record notes that the managed job runner remains provisioned and idle and that its credentials were rotated after the rollback.
state.claim_a: Priya Raghavan carried out the rollback of the billing scheduler change.
state.claim_b: The duplicate job identifiers were caused by clock skew between the two hosts.
state.claim_c: Customer invoices were delayed by change CR-4482.
